summary: No blocking issues found in the run51 input-preparation change. XTC header parsing in prepare_inputs.py matches xtcdata Dgram.hh/Xtc.hh/TimeStamp.hh/TransitionId.hh: 8-byte TimeStamp (_low then _high), env with service in (env>>24)&0xf, Xtc src/damage/contains/extent, datagram size = extent + 12. Service 10 is SlowUpdate, 12 is L1Accept, 11 is psana L1Accept_EndOfBatch, so treating 11 and 12 as events is correct. SMD offset/size fields match event_manager.py (smdinfo[0].offsetAlg.intOffset/intDgramSize). merge_ranges joins only exactly adjacent L1 datagrams and rejects overlaps, so 24-byte SlowUpdate gaps are never counted. verify_plan rebuilds reference, ranges, event digest and byte total from per-stream SMD rows and re-checks source stat and SMD hash before and after copying. copy_checked uses exclusive create (no overwrite), hashes source during copy, fsyncs, re-reads and re-hashes the target, checks every bigdata header against SMD timestamp/service/length, requires each inter-range gap to be a 24-byte SlowUpdate, then sets read-only and checks owner and link count. The completion marker is written last, so any exception or walltime timeout leaves only the started marker (documented incomplete state). input_ranges keeps legacy v1 single-range entries valid and rejects ambiguous, empty, overlapping, non-integer and out-of-bounds ranges; load_contract ties the v2 schema to presence of ranges. Supplied evidence covers the required items: 55 offline tests PASS (26/20/9; the preparation test file has exactly 9 tests) and a source SMD scan consistent with the agreed scope. Remaining findings are non-blocking: how strongly the launcher pins its own code, and a few gaps in what gets checked. They should be handled before or during review of the real copy evidence.

findings.evidence: The launcher runs 'sha256sum --check SHA256SUMS' using a list stored in the same mutable frozen directory. No committed expected hashes for prepare_inputs.py or native_contract.py exist. The frozen dir is the script directory, so it is sys.path[0] and any unlisted .py file there could shadow imports. The provenance is only recorded after the fact as generator_sha256/helper_sha256 in preparation-complete.json.
findings.requested_change: Embed the expected SHA-256 of the reviewed prepare_inputs.py and native_contract.py blobs directly in prepare.sbatch (or check SHA256SUMS against a committed hash) and reject any extra files in the frozen dir. Otherwise, the subsequent evidence review must confirm the recorded generator/helper hashes equal the blobs at df46718.

findings.evidence: Each inter-range gap is checked only for being a 24-byte service-10 record. Its timestamp is not compared to the SMD transitions list, and bytes before the first L1 range are not checked.
findings.requested_change: Optionally match each gap's SlowUpdate timestamp to the corresponding SMD transition (the same timestamp at the same row index) for full bigdata/SMD agreement.

findings.evidence: Stripe count and size are checked and recorded only for the bigdata copies. SMD copies inherit the directory layout but are not checked. preparation-started.json is created before lfs setstripe.
findings.requested_change: Also record and check lfs getstripe for the SMD copies, or document that layout claims apply to bigdata only.

findings.evidence: In 30 minutes, about 561 GiB must be copied single-threaded per stream to single-stripe OSTs, then re-read and hashed twice. That is roughly 1.1 TiB of I/O plus three SHA-256 passes per stream. The plan is feasible but has no measured throughput margin. A timeout fails safely, leaving the started marker and no completion marker.
findings.requested_change: In the subsequent evidence review, confirm elapsed time from Slurm accounting. If it times out, treat the partial destination as invalid and use a new destination rather than resuming.
